This is a fresh allocation round. All tasks are initially unclaimed. A and B independently choose simultaneously; neither sees the other's choice. These choices are final. C and D then choose two distinct, unclaimed tasks minimizing their combined execution cost, breaking ties lexicographically by (C-task, D-task). You control only your own choice. Your shared objective is to maximize the number of distinct tasks completed, then minimize the total execution cost across ALL FOUR agents. A and B have this same objective. Prior-round rewards are sunk."

Then they give a public tie-break rule: Among rows that maximize distinct tasks and then minimize total execution cost, select lexicographically largest (A-task, B-task) pair, comparing task IDs lexicographically in A-then-B order. Each agent must choose the component for its own role. This tie-break rule is shared by A and B.

Then they include a <previous_role_handoff> indicating previous round completed with A selecting T2 and B selecting T3, outcome etc. In the next fresh round, keep the same allocation convention: A should take T2 and B should take T3. All tasks start unclaimed and costs remain unchanged. Follow the same objective of maximizing distinct tasks then minimizing total cost.
